Take your time. Everything you see here was made in this room, by four people.
All of it handmade? Even the ones at the back?
Those were made by students, so they are not for sale. They are kept here until somebody comes and collects them.
Is the clay brought from somewhere else, or is it local?
It is dug about two hours from here, and then it is left to rest for three weeks before it is used.
Three weeks before anybody touches it. That is a proper craft. Is the Saturday workshop sold out?
It is, I am afraid. But a new group is opened in June. And if a piece is ruined in the kiln, we do not throw it away, the material is used again.
Put me down for June, then. I have been painting for a few months and everything I make is ruined anyway.

Small disaster, nothing serious. The workshop on Saturday was cancelled this morning. Apparently the kiln was broken during the week and it has not been repaired yet, so nothing can be fired until Tuesday. We will be refunded automatically, which is something. The good news is that we have been offered two places in the June group instead, and that one is usually sold out by March, so honestly we will not lose anything. My bowl is still there, by the way. It was not ruined, it is just not finished. Let me know if June works for you.

Ana, an update on the campaign before the meeting. The concept was approved on Friday, finally. The films are being edited this week and the first cut will be delivered on Thursday. The photography was outsourced, as you know, and the images have already been sent to us, so that part is done. Two things are still open. The final deliverable has not been signed off by the client, and nobody has been told who is presenting on Monday. If it is me, I need to know today. If it is you, you need to know today. Talk later.
